questions.question: How do union types and type narrowing work in TypeScript?
questions.title: Typescript Unions Narrowing
questions.direct_answer: A union type (string | number) means the value is one of those members — at any point, only the common operations are safe. Narrowing is the compiler following control flow to refine the type: typeof checks narrow primitives, instanceof narrows classes, in checks narrow by property presence, truthiness and equality checks narrow anything, and discriminated unions (a literal 'kind' tag) narrow by the tag's value. Checked narrowing unlocks member-specific operations the union wouldn't allow.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U[union: string bar number] --> G{typeof guard}
    G -->|string| S[string branch - .toUpperCase safe]
    G -->|number| N[number branch - .toFixed safe]
    D[discriminated: kind tag] --> SW{switch kind}
    SW -->|circle| C[r available]
    SW -->|rect| R[w h available]
    SW -->|default| NEV[never - exhaustiveness proof]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Control-flow analysis (how narrowing actually works): TS's checker tracks types through branches, assignments, and returns. Narrowing composes: a typeof inside a loop narrows until an assignment can change the type, at which point the flow analysis widens it again. The analysis is per-variable — narrowing one variable of a union doesn't narrow another (unless you use a type predicate).

The exhaustiveness guarantee (the depth marker): with a discriminated union and a switch over the tag, the never type proves exhaustiveness — add `default: const _never: never = s;` and the compiler ERRORS if you add a new variant and forget the case. Without the default, a missed case returns undefined silently. The pattern: exhaustive switches + never-assertions turn 'did you handle all the cases?' from a code-review question into a compile error — the same guarantee Redux reducer authors seek with default-cases.

The boundary of narrowing (what it can't do): narrowing is syntactic — it follows checks the COMPILER can see in the current function. Extract the check into an untyped helper (`function isString(x) { return typeof x === 'string' }`) and the narrowing is LOST at the call site — the fix is type predicates: `function isString(x): x is string`. That's what type guards ARE: user-defined functions that extend the flow analysis. Assertion signatures (asserts x is T) are the throwing variant.
